resources.string: Let us add it to your medicines.
A medicine a doctor prescribed is added in today’s chat, with the day it starts.
For questions about a medicine, a pharmacist can help, and the leaflet that came with it says what to avoid.
What is it called? You can type the name as it is on the box.
I do not know its name
Is it one of your medicines?
%1$s starts on %2$s in your medicines, so this dose is recorded on its own.
%1$s is no longer in your medicines, so it can be noted on its own instead.
Which of today’s doses was it?
Today’s doses of %1$s are already marked: %2$s.
%1$s was noted at %2$s. Is this another dose?
That time has not come yet today. When did you take it?
For example, 10 ml or half a tablet
What did you take it for?
The pain noted in this chat says no painkiller was taken today. Change that to yes?
Is that more than the packet or leaflet says to take, at once or in 24 hours?
Is that more than your prescription says?
Before anything else: have you taken more of a medicine than the packet, leaflet or prescription says?

Please get medical advice now from an urgent medical helpline, even if you feel well. If you are told to go to an emergency department, do not drive: ask someone to take you, or call emergency services. Take the packet or leaflet with you, and any other medicines you take.
Do you have any of these now: a fast or uneven heartbeat, a fit, feeling very drowsy or passing out, difficulty breathing, or sudden confusion?
Do you have any of these now: difficulty breathing or short, shallow breathing, a fit, or feeling so sleepy it is hard to stay awake?
Do you have any of these now: difficulty breathing or short, shallow breathing; a fit; feeling very drowsy or passing out; a fast or uneven heartbeat; sudden confusion?
How have you been feeling since you started %1$s?
It is not common, but some people starting %1$s have thoughts of harming themselves or of not wanting to live. Have you had thoughts like that since you started it?
Thoughts of harming yourself or of not wanting to live
Feeling unusually high, or full of energy
A fast heartbeat with sweating, shaking, twitching muscles, or feeling confused or agitated
Unexplained bruising or bleeding, or blood in your pee, poo or vomit
A swollen throat or tongue, or difficulty breathing
Passing out, a fit, chest pain, or sudden weakness, numbness or trouble speaking
Please get medical advice now from an urgent medical helpline. Keep the medicine’s leaflet with you.
Side effects that bother you or do not go away are worth talking over with a pharmacist or your doctor. Keep taking it unless you are told to stop.
Please do not take two doses to make up for a missed one. The leaflet says what to do about a missed dose, and a pharmacist can tell you if you are not sure.
The leaflet that came with it says what to do about a missed dose; if you are not sure, ask a pharmacist.
Nothing is noted, so the %1$s dose stays unmarked.
Nothing is noted, so the dose on waking stays unmarked.
That dose was already marked at %1$s, so nothing new is noted.
It is best not to drink alcohol with %1$s. The leaflet says more.
With %1$s it is best to keep alcohol low. The leaflet says more.
The guidance for %1$s says that with alcohol it can make you more sleepy. It may be best to avoid alcohol until you know how the medicine affects you.
The guidance for these medicines says %1$s and %2$s may not mix well. A pharmacist can check the medicines you take together.
Guidance for %1$s says not to use St John’s wort while taking it. Please talk to a pharmacist or your doctor.
The guidance for %1$s and %2$s says which painkillers not to take at the same time. A pharmacist can check these two for you.
Two medicines that both contain paracetamol should not be taken at the same time, as that can mean taking too much. Please check the packets of %1$s and %2$s, or ask a pharmacist.
Two medicines that contain an opioid painkiller, such as codeine or tramadol, are not taken together. Please check the packets of %1$s and %2$s, or ask a pharmacist.
The guidance for %1$s says that, taken with opioid painkillers, it can make you very drowsy and affect your breathing. Please ask a pharmacist or your doctor whether to take it with %2$s.
The guidance for these medicines says %1$s and %2$s are not taken together. Please talk to a pharmacist or your doctor.
If you take other medicines regularly, a pharmacist can check that %1$s goes with them.
Is it a medicine you take every day? It can be added to your medicines, with reminders.
%1$s · the dose on waking · marked at %2$s
%1$s · %2$s · at %3$s · not part of a schedule
%1$s · %2$s · on %3$s · not part of a schedule
What is the medicine called? You can type the name as it is on the box or the prescription.
I do not know the name yet
A medicine is added with its name. Once you know it, tell the chat, or add it on the Medicine tab.
%1$s is already in your medicines: %2$s. What has changed?
Nothing, it is the same one
The dose and the times are changed on its own page, so the doses already marked keep their record.
Did your doctor tell you to stop it?
No, it is my own decision
Please do not stop taking it suddenly, or without talking to your doctor first. A doctor can help plan how to stop.
Stopping can bring withdrawal symptoms, sometimes feeling very low or suicidal. If that happens, speak to your doctor; if you might not be safe, call emergency services.
The day it ends is set on its page.
%1$s was in your medicines until %2$s. This adds it again as a new course.
What dose does the box or the prescription say? For example, 50 mg or 1 tablet.
More than three times a day
How should it be noted, then?
Add it as a daily course
The medicine list keeps medicines taken on a schedule, with reminders. A medicine taken only when needed can be added as a daily course, or each dose noted when it is taken.
For now the medicine list keeps only daily times, so it would remind you every day. Each dose can also be noted here when it is taken.
At what times? Tap the times that are right, or add your own.
Does it say anything about food?
Today’s %1$s dose has already gone by. Has it been taken?
Today’s dose on waking: has it been taken?
Today’s doses at %1$s have already gone by. Which have been taken?
As its time has passed, its reminder will sound as soon as it is added.
The %1$s dose will show as not taken today until it is marked.
The doses at %1$s will show as not taken today until they are marked.
The answer goes into the medicine’s note.
Today’s %1$s dose is marked as taken.
Today’s doses at %1$s are marked as taken.
It will remind you after you wake.
Reminders are switched off in the app, so nothing will remind you about it. Turn them on? That also turns on the reminders for food, water, steps and the journal.
Reminders stay off. The medicine is in your list, and its doses can be marked there or here.
Notifications from the app are off on this phone, so a reminder cannot show.
Notifications are still off, so no reminder can show.

Exact alarms are still off, so a reminder may come a few minutes late.

It is not common, but some people have suicidal thoughts or an urge to harm themselves when they start %1$s. If that happens, speak to a doctor straight away. If you might not be safe, call emergency services.
It is not common, but some people taking %1$s have thoughts of harming themselves or of ending their life. If that happens, call emergency services or go to an emergency department.
